videos.title: I Left My Mafia Husband to Rot. Now He’s in My Cage.
videos.description:
Thirty minutes in the freezing rain. That was all the time it took to turn my untouchable mafia surgeon into a caged ghost. 🌧️🩸

When I found Julian’s smashed BMW on Route 9, his radiator screaming steam into the midnight downpour, I didn't rush him to the emergency bay. I rolled down my window just far enough to catch the coppery stench of spilled arterial blood and hot motor oil. I looked right into the eyes of the man who spent six months fucking his high-society trauma surgeon, embezzling three million dollars from my late father’s syndicate to buy an oceanfront escape villa in Costa Rica—and I calmly told the shivering college bystanders I had an emergency. 

I drove five hundred meters down the blacktop, pulled over at a dark weigh station, and watched the digital clock glow green on the dashboard. I timed the ischemia down to the second. Julian was the one who taught me human anatomy across my father’s billiard table when we were teenagers; he was the one who told me that when spinal gray matter is deprived of perfusion, the neurons suffocate in thirty minutes. I didn't murder him. I just made sure his spine drowned in its own necrotic acid. ⏳🥀

Now, the sharp, arrogant surgeon who thought he could outrun the Moretti family is wheeled into my brownstone on a titanium frame. I am the devoted, self-sacrificing mob wife who feeds him, changes his leg bags, crushes ninety milligrams of sedatives into his morning tea, and adjusts his motorized bed to pinch his bruised ribs. And when he finally cornered me in the dark with a tumbler of rye, demanding why I left him in the dirt, I leaned down and whispered the truth against his lips: I was sixteen when I stood behind the grandfather clock and watched him shove my father down twenty-four marble stairs. I didn't marry him out of love; I married him as a seven-year execution. 🖤🦽

Stripping his mistress of her medical license and exiling her to the mud, I had Julian permanently committed to the stone fortress of Blackwood Psychiatric Facility under my sole legal conservatorship. Locked inside that cold granite rotunda, his ruined fingers pressed against the pulse of my wrist, realizing the horrifying, inescapable truth: we are two monsters forged in the same slaughterhouse. We destroyed each other, but across iron bars, paralysis, and madness, neither of us will ever let the other go. 🗝️🏛️

I lost my memory. Who are you?"

Dante does not flinch. With terrifying speed and raw physical dominance, he sweeps her off her feet, slamming her lower back against his cold mahogany desk and pinning her wrists flat against the blotter. videos.title: "You Look Pathetic Without Me," My Mafia Ex Sneered—While Tearing My Wig Exposed My Bare Head
videos.description:
Standing in the damp morning mist of St. Jude's Memorial Cemetery on All Souls' Day, I was negotiating a five-percent promotional discount on my own hillside burial plot. Shaved completely bald for a high-risk palliative craniotomy scheduled in four weeks, I was wearing an unapologetic, blazing crimson synthetic wig—a symbol of fierce survival gifted by my best friend.

Then, three armored black Cadillacs tore through the cemetery gates.

From the rear door stepped Adrian Moretti—the undisputed, lethal Don of Boston's most entrenched crime syndicate. Sneering in bitter disgust at my frayed denim jacket and vibrant hair, he towered over me, his voice dripping with venom: "Did you fall so low after leaving me, Elena? Did you end up this pathetic without my money?" With cruel arrogance, he reached out and violently ripped my hair.

With a sickening tear, the crimson wig flew into the muddy gravel, landing among dead leaves and burnt incense ash—exposing my bare, shaved skull and the stark purple surgical incision crosshatched across my skin.

Adrian froze, the color draining from his face as his eyes locked onto my bald head, my hospital envelope labeled "Terminal Recurrent Glioblastoma," and the cemetery deed in my hands. But before he could speak, I looked up with a deadpan smile and extended my phone: "Two hundred and fifty dollars, you absolute jerk. Pay up."

He didn't know the horrifying truth.

Three years ago, when Adrian believed I took a five-hundred-thousand-dollar buyout from his ruthless father and vanished, I was actually dying on an emergency operating table with status epilepticus. I spent thirty days comatose, waking up with my memories wiped clean, an uncashed check I never spent, and hundreds of venomous messages from a stranger ending in 8888 whom I blocked as a scammer.

Now, with weeks left to live, the billionaire mob boss who spent three years cursing my name discovers that the woman he branded a mercenary traitor never took a single dime of his fortune.

When Adrian mobilizes the entire wealth of the Moretti empire, shaving his own head to match mine, peeling ninety-nine unbroken apples to bargain with saints, and putting his own life on the line against syndicate traitors to keep me breathing, the greatest battle of our lives begins. But can fifty million dollars and a repentant Don defeat an incurable clock inside my brain?

videos.title: My Billionaire Mother Cursed Me As A Monster, Unaware I Stabbed Her To Trade My Life For Hers
videos.description:
Thirteen years ago, when Don Robert DeLuca’s heavily armed extraction unit stormed our derelict Appalachian hideout, my mother—the long-lost heiress to Boston’s most powerful pharmaceutical and criminal syndicate—reached out with weeping eyes: "Sweetheart, come home with Mama."

Instead of crying in relief, I violently wrenched my wrist away, grabbed a rusted hunting knife, and slashed her arm. 

I cursed her as an ungrateful jinx, demanding thirty thousand dollars in cold blood money to buy out our motherhood: "Give me thirty grand, or I’ll tell the federal prosecutors the billionaire DeLuca heiress abandoned her lawful family!" 

Horrified and shattered by my unprovoked cruelty, my mother threw a certified draft at my feet, declaring: "Thirty thousand dollars. We are dead to each other." My mafia grandfather sneered that an abusive cartel mongrel would always breed filth. 

They never knew the horrifying truth. 

In my first life, I had followed my mother back to Boston. But my presence as a cartel bastard disgraced her in high society, stripped her of her corporate inheritance, and caused her to be ambushed and murdered on the street by my abusive father. Grief-stricken, I carried her ashes back to the mountains, offering my own soul and second lifetime to an ancient dark shaman: a life for a life, so that Sophia DeLuca could be reborn into wealth, dignity, and absolute glory. 

And that knife wound? It was carefully angled to bleed heavily without severing a tendon—a calculated sacrifice to ensure my mother severed all ties with me, climbed the corporate ladder, and reclaimed her rightful throne as the undisputed CEO of DeLuca Bio-Pharma.

Now, thirteen years later, the cosmic debt has come to collect. I am twenty-five, living in a crumbling East Boston tenement, diagnosed with an inoperable, terminal Grade IV glioblastoma. 

When my abusive cartel father is released on parole and threatens to butcher Sophia unless I hand over two million dollars, I refuse to let the cycle repeat. I sew a digital voice recorder into my coat lapel, deliberately provoke his murderous rage, and let him plunge his eight-inch blade into my chest while smashing my skull against a cast-iron radiator—rupturing my fatal brain tumor, but locking my dying arms around his legs until tactical police swarm the room.

In the neuro-ICU at Massachusetts General Hospital, as my brainstem herniates and the monitors begin to flatline, Sophia DeLuca hears the bloody recording. She finds my legal name-change decree, my clean bank ledgers, and my untreated terminal pathology report. She realizes that every cruel word, every demand, and that single bleeding stab thirteen years ago was the desperate, holy sacrifice of a daughter who loved her enough to die twice for her crown.

A breathtaking, devastating tale of maternal devotion, mafia blood debts, and the ultimate sacrifice of a girl who made herself a monster so her mother could become a queen.

videos.title: "I Hope You Die A Horrible Death," My Mafia Ex Cursed—While My Cold Corpse Froze Below
videos.description:
For twenty-five years, Julian DeLuca lived among the clouds. He was the golden heir to New England's most powerful pharmaceutical dynasty, a reclusive prodigy at Harvard Medical School who saw the world through sterile formulas. Until he defied his syndicate bloodline and married me—a girl from the South Boston slums whose mind was poisoned by unspeakable childhood horrors. 

When my suffocating, untreated paranoia tore our life apart, Julian filed for divorce. In a blind panic, terrified of losing my only light, I drugged his soup and chained him inside the master bedroom suite of our Beacon Hill brownstone for thirty days. 

During that month of captivity, he pleaded, he broke, and finally, he cursed me with raw, venomous hatred: "You're a sick monster, Clara! I hope you die a horrible death!" 

When the police finally kicked down the doors to rescue him, Julian stood before flashing media cameras, lip bleeding, swearing to the press: "She’s a lunatic. Even if she drops dead, we are divorced."

He didn't know that his curse had already been answered. 

Two floors beneath his feet, my body had been rotting in a hidden sub-basement bunker for forty-eight hours. 

And when Julian finally uncovers the sealed police records, he learns the truth that shatters his sanity: I didn't lock him up to torture him. To me, mental institutions were the places where they strapped me down and fried my brain with electricity. And in that dark bunker, I had hooked a homemade step-up transformer directly to my own heart, trying desperately to "shock the madness out of my chest" so I could be a normal, loving wife he could introduce to the world. My dying, frozen hand was found reaching toward a phone charger—trying to dial 911 so he wouldn't starve before help arrived.

Wrecked by guilt, Julian discovers an even darker secret: he never wanted to divorce me. He had filed the petition only because Massachusetts law required it to establish a private conservatorship and send me to a luxury clinic in Zurich. Unable to bear the reality of his own blind cruelty, the brilliant professor synthesizes an unlicensed, lethal neuro-compound, chemically poisoning his own brain receptors just so he can hallucinate my ghost beside him in the passenger seat. 

A devastating, poignant dark-romance tale of generational trauma, misplaced devotion, and the heartbreaking truth that some wounds can never be healed in time.

My new boyfriend had just returned from a four-day syndicate summit in Miami. We were tangled on the master suite sofa, breathless, clothing half-shed, lost in an intoxicating reunion.

Then, the unlatched door clicked open.

Standing in the threshold, frozen in tailored navy pinstripes, was Julian DeLuca—the golden heir of the eastern seaboard, the boy I had spent seven years tutoring, bleeding for, and worshipping in high school, only to be kept in the humiliating purgatory of the "friend zone" while he chased another heiress.

When Julian recognized my face, the color drained from his skin until he looked like a walking corpse. He gripped his leather portfolio so hard his knuckles turned white, forcing out a strained, ghastly whisper: "Looks like I came at the wrong time."

My boyfriend didn't scramble. He didn't hide.

Dante Romano—the lethal, illegitimate sovereign of the five boroughs who called Julian brother—pulled his heavy overcoat over my bare thighs, looked Julian dead in the eye, and deliberately lowered his mouth to my throat. Right in front of the man who had discarded me five years ago, Dante pressed a searing, possessive kiss into the soft hollow of my bare neck: "Don't be scared, baby. He's my brother. He won't bite."

In that single, electric second, five years of unrequited agony shattered into pure, unadulterated triumph.

Julian had spent half a decade scouring the continent for the quiet tutor who had walked away, hoarding a dried gardenia flower in his glove compartment like a dying monk. Now, watching his closest brother claim my skin, the regret turned into unhinged madness. He crashed his Mercedes into a highway guardrail, weeping blood onto the steering wheel, begging to know if I truly didn't want him anymore. He fabricated fifty-million-dollar maritime contracts just to see my face, and dropped to his knees on my welcome mat in the pouring rain, pleading to be my dog.

But some awakenings arrive five years too late. Dante Romano had bled his own veins dry taking a hollow-point bullet for me in Rome, and a woman who has finally been crowned by a true king never crawls back to beg for scraps from a coward.

Ten years ago, on a graduation trip to Lake Tahoe, I fell madly in love with Dante DeLuca, believing our romance was the start of an unbreakable dynasty. 

I had no idea it was a calculated execution. 

Two days before I was to enter university, Dante walked into my father's academy office, casually flipped a positive pregnancy test onto the mahogany desk, and sneered: 
"Dean Lin, your daughter carries my child. The blood is mine, but I am dumping her."

He vanished into the rain, leaving my father in catastrophic disgrace. My father, a man who had preached spotless virtue his entire life, ran blindly into the stormy traffic in despair and was crushed by a truck. My mother suffered a total breakdown, her mind shattered, her kidneys failing. 

For ten long years, I raised our son Leo alone in an unheated tenement, scrubbing floors and enduring cold transactions just to pay for my mother's dialysis and my son's schoolbooks. 

Ten years later, I encountered Dante again. He was now the ruthless Don of the eastern syndicate, engaged to an elite heiress. He sneered at my poverty, until he discovered that my father died on the day of his revenge, my mother was in an asylum, and our nine-year-old son was his spitting image.

When the medical truth struck—advanced stage-four lymphoma with six months to live—the untouchable crime boss collapsed on his knees, weeping in the hospital corridor, begging to trade his entire fortune just to save my life.

I didn't waste my breath on anger. I used his crushing guilt as the ultimate shield, having him marry me and sign over his multi-million-dollar dynasty to our son. And when my boy was forever safe, I closed my eyes in peace, ready to fly free like a butterfly into the golden dawn.

videos.title: "She Was Just A Bet," My Mafia Husband Laughed—And Morning Chills Froze My Numb Ankles
videos.description:
At nineteen, I believed Matteo Romano when he whispered that I was his only sanctuary in the dark. 

The very next morning, standing in the cold hallway holding a bag of warm custard pastries, I heard his voice through the slightly ajar door: 
"Chloe Vance? A bet is a bet. Did you honestly think I could fall for a rigid bookworm like her? She was like wood. Don't forget to split the five hundred dollars."

I didn't storm in. I didn't shed a single tear. I simply dropped his steaming breakfast into the trash can and put on the mask of the perfect, obedient girlfriend. 

For four years, Matteo flaunted his wealth, his power, and his women across the five boroughs, boasting to his capos that I was so addicted to his touch I could never leave. He never suspected the truth: every time I touched his face in the dark, I was not seeing him at all. 

He looked seventy percent identical to Christian Walker—the brave, undercover detective who gave his life to protect me, murdered because my venomous sister exposed his face to the cartel. Matteo was never my lover. He was only a dead hero's hollow reflection.

When the truth finally exploded across his seven-thousand-square-foot penthouse, the untouchable Don lost his mind, tearing his empire to shreds. But when he finally begged on his knees in the pouring rain, carving another man's tear mole into his own bleeding flesh just to be my substitute, it was already too late.

The dawn was coming. And I was going home to the only man I ever loved.

"Clara, you should be thrilling with joy right now. A girl from your low-class gutter getting to sleep in my bed for two years is pure dumb luck—you ought to fall on your knees and thank God for the privilege." For two agonizing years, Clara Vance pinched every single penny, skipped meals, and worked herself to exhaustion to support her boyfriend, believing he was a penniless student striving for a decent future. But the man she loved was actually Dante Moretti—the ruthless, billionaire heir to the most powerful crime syndicate on the Eastern Seaboard. When she uncovered his secret and confronted him, he laughed in her face, pointed to a five-thousand-dollar bottle of vintage wine, and discarded her like garbage.

Three years later, in the dim hallway of an exclusive Manhattan lounge, a sharp, resounding slap shatters the quiet—leaving an angry crimson handprint burning across a cheek that thought it was untouchable. While Dante Moretti fought a savage, three-year war through the underworld to seize absolute power, break his dynastic engagement, and crown Clara as his queen, he forgot one fatal truth: you cannot buy back a woman's shattered soul with stolen billions.

When Dante desperately corners her on Fifth Avenue, boasting of his supreme authority, Clara pulls out a worn, three-year-old velvet box containing a modest quarter-carat ring—a simple white-gold band she had secretly bought with her own life savings to propose to him when she thought he was poor and struggling. In a blind rage of possessive arrogance, Dante mocks it as worthless plastic and hurls it straight down a sewer storm drain... only to discover three days later that he threw his own salvation into the gutter.

A woman's greatest victory is never winning back the man who crushed her, nor is it inheriting his empire when his heart stops beating. Her greatest victory is the quiet, unbreakable courage to walk away, reclaim her dignity, and author her own destiny.

I followed Dante Cole when I was eighteen, enduring fifty lashes from my family's syndicate whip and taking two bullets in a warehouse ambush that scarred my womb and left me barren—all to help a gutter brawler become the undisputed King of Atlantic City.
Ten years later, his twenty-two-year-old mistress, Bianca Bell, marched into our oceanfront estate with a pregnant belly. Dante shielded her, coldly demanding I pretend nothing happened because she could give him the heir I never could.
When I slapped the divorce papers across his face, Dante snapped. He pinned my throat against the wall, eyes bloodshot with manic fury, snarling that divorce was impossible—that I would either stay and die with him, or he would slaughter everyone and blow his own brains out over my grave.
Then Bianca sent me a video: Dante holding her hand during prenatal checkups, whispering that I was too dirty from killing and that my bloodstained hands disgusted him.
He forgot who built his throne. He forgot that every casino license, every shipping lane, and every enforcer he commanded answered to the daughter of Don Antonio Moretti.
I burned our marital mansion to the ground and revoked the divorce. A clean break was far too merciful.
I intercepted his two-billion-dollar casino concession, fixed his two-hundred-million-dollar underground cage fight, and leaked his cryptographic ledgers to federal prosecutors. When Dante discovered Bianca was merely an unacknowledged illegitimate child with zero legal claim to my father's sovereign billions, he fell to his knees in tears, begging for mercy.
I looked at him with icy indifference: "Kneel and beg."

videos.title: "Take Ten Million And Go," My Mafia Husband Sneered—Before I Erased His Ten-Billion Empire
videos.description:
After eleven years of standing by his side, helping him rise from a penniless street orphan into the fifteen-billion-dollar kingpin of New York's tech underworld, my husband poured his morning coffee and calmly demanded a divorce.
His reason? He wanted to give his twenty-two-year-old marketing intern, Chloe Evans, a proper title and high-society wedding. 
Outside the municipal registry, Marcus habitually tucked a stray lock of hair behind my ear with the gentle reflex of a decade, then tossed a black titanium card onto the stone balustrade with an arrogant smirk: "Take ten million and go. You can't survive without my protection."
He truly believed I was a helpless vine that would wither without his charity. He never knew that his empire, his proprietary neural defense code, his European naval port concessions, and his angel capital were never the result of his own genius. 
They were Project Polaris—a shadow fortress I had secretly built for him while rejecting my own father's thirty-billion-dollar sovereign throne.
The moment our divorce decree was stamped, I initiated the protocol. I wiped the root encryption algorithms, severed his international logistics channels, and recalled our elite technical architects. 
Within fourteen days, his fifteen-billion-dollar empire imploded. His stock crashed, creditors seized his penthouses and supercars, and the young intern he traded me for ransacked his emergency safe and left him penniless in a Queens basement.
When Marcus finally found my old leather journal and discovered the bloodstained truth of who had truly held the sky above his head, he broke. In front of five thousand delegates, dignitaries, and cameras at the Metropolitan Museum, he fell to his knees in the mud, weeping and begging for forgiveness.

I didn't even look him in the eye. I simply linked arms with Adrian Stone, the sovereign billionaire who had loved me through eleven years of silence, and murmured that the security was rather substandard.

videos.title: "Abort the baby and I'll forgive you," my mob husband scoffed. I slid the hidden divorce papers.
videos.description:
When my billionaire mafia husband returned home at midnight smelling of fresh eucalyptus shower gel, I didn't question his corporate overtime.

I simply pushed my twelve-week ultrasound report across the marble table.

Sean Moretti froze, his pupils contracting in shock. Assuming I had cheated because we used protection for two years and hadn't been intimate in six months, he slumped onto the sofa with a cold, dismissive sneer: "Abort it, and I'll overlook it."

I looked into his eyes and whispered: "The child is yours. Conceived using your cryo-preserved sample the exact morning your secretary, Natalie Ross, reached forty-two days of pregnancy and you escorted her to her private clinic."

As his face turned the color of wet chalk, I reached beneath the sofa cushion and slid our divorce agreement across the table: "Sign it, Sean. We end this cleanly."

An orphan raised in Queens, I entered our marriage viewing love as a strategic ledger. When I discovered his affair two years ago, I didn't scream or make a scene. I waited. Over eight hundred days, I earned an Executive MBA, built my venture fund into an eighteen-billion-dollar sovereign powerhouse, and waited for his guilt to mature.

When Sean violently shredded the divorce papers and staged a desperate, week-long courtship to revive our college romance, an anonymous whistleblower leaked high-resolution photographs of him and his mistress on a private yacht.

With the syndicate stock in freefall, I took the podium at an international press conference, announcing that Sean and I had quietly divorced two years ago, shielding the family assets while securing fifteen percent of his voting equity for our unborn twins.

videos.title: "That Is Your Real Brother," My Mafia Brother Sneered—While Pointing To A Dying Stranger
videos.description:
My brother hated me for seven agonizing years.

When our parents died in an earthquake seven years ago, my brother Christian convinced himself that my survival was a crime. After our final explosive argument, I walked out into a freezing rainstorm, fell from the Manhattan Bridge, and woke up in Mount Sinai Hospital with acute concussion and dissociative memory confusion.

Instead of relief, Christian felt delight. Eager to sever all blood ties, he looked across the crowded hospital corridor, pointed at a terminally ill stranger leaning against the wall, and sneered: "That is your real brother over there. Look carefully, don't scream at me, and never bother me again."

As Christian turned his back and walked away, the pale, dying stranger stepped forward. He did not curse or call security. With astonishing tenderness, he placed his warm palm on my head and whispered: "Then let's go. Brother is taking you home."

That stranger was Julian Sterling, the brilliant twenty-eight-year-old tech billionaire who had stunned Wall Street by liquidating his empire. But inside his empty, cold modern villa, Julian was silently waiting to die of end-stage congestive heart failure—living alone with prescription sleeping pills and his own framed obituary portrait, grieving the little sister who had taken her life years ago to save him money.

Two broken souls, discarded by their blood relatives, made a sacred covenant in the dark: to fight for life.

When an organ donor match is discovered in Norway, Clara refuses to let Julian die. Discovering that the world's preeminent transplant surgeon, Dr. Robert Wei, is visiting his elderly mother in a snowbound Adirondack valley, Clara treks nine miles alone through a thirty-five-below mountain blizzard, collapsing half-frozen in the snowdrifts to beg for Julian's life.

For five years, I lived in the shadows of the Moretti empire, managing Luca’s logistics, shielding his secrets, and watching him rise from a ruthless underboss to the supreme Don of the five boroughs.

At 2:17 a.m. outside an upstate estate, I watched through the tinted glass of our armored Maybach as he paraded Gianna Bellini before the cameras. When he stepped into the cold rain, he didn't even look at my face. He ordered me to pour the hot seafood broth I had simmered for hours into a cup for his glamorous new companion. 

At 3:30 a.m. in our cold Manhattan penthouse, I finally asked what would happen if I stopped waiting. Luca buttoned his cuffs, picked up his car keys, and delivered a cold, casual ultimatum: 
"Elena, if you don't want to wait, we are done."

He walked out the door to spend the night at Gianna’s hotel suite. 

I didn't scream. I didn't beg. I packed my half-empty suitcase, emailed my formal resignation, blocked every syndicate line, and boarded an early morning flight to Boston to reclaim my life. 

In Boston, I found an independent creative agency, earning my own success under the sun, and met Julian DeLuca—a brilliant, gentle man who had silently loved me for three years, cherishing the ground I walked on.

When Luca finally realized that his empire was crumbling without the woman who built it, the powerful Don came begging in the freezing wind, weeping on his knees, offering marriage and millions. But some loves arrive too late. And a woman who has finally stepped into the sunlight never crawls back into the dark.

videos.description:
At 11:42 p.m. during a brutal Chicago blizzard, I lay bleeding on a freezing operating table at Rush University Medical Center while the pre-op nurse dialed my Mafia husband Matteo Moretti for the fourth time. Twelve weeks pregnant after three agonizing years of IVF, I had slipped on the icy steps he left unlatched when he rushed out to comfort his childhood sweetheart, Camila Costa. He never answered the hospital switchboard. Instead, he texted me two words of cold dismissal—"Be reasonable"—while Camila posted a photo from the eighth-floor VIP suite just three floors above my operating room, showing my husband tenderly spoon-feeding her warm broth over a mild fever.

I did not scream, and I did not beg. Before the surgical lamps clicked on without general anesthesia, I asked the nurse for the clipboard, crossed Matteo Moretti off my emergency contact form, and replaced his name with my brother's. By seven o'clock the next morning, every diamond Matteo had ever bought me and my three-carat engagement ring sat neatly beside my hospital admission band on the coffee table of our empty Gold Coast penthouse. He thought I was just throwing a jealous tantrum and would crawl back within three days—until Camila showed up waving a surprise pregnancy ultrasound, my structural engineering license was pulled from his forty-five-million-dollar port contract, and my lawyer walked into Don Robert Moretti's seventieth birthday banquet carrying three velvet presentation boxes that exposed a five-year medical secret.

What would you have done if you were in Elena's shoes on that snowy night at the hospital? Would you have walked away in silence, or waited for the family council banquet to reveal the truth? "Too filthy, scatter her ashes. A woman like her does not deserve a grave." When the mortuary handed my cremated remains to my ruthless Mafia husband, Dante Moretti tapped the marble urn with the only smile he had shown all day—and then turned his hand over, shattering my urn across the granite steps and grinding his heel into my ashes as my brother wept on his knees.



For six years, Dante believed my wealthy family had orchestrated the hit-and-run that killed his first love, Camilla, just to transplant her heart into my failing chest. To avenge her, he married me, locked me away in a secluded hillside villa, and drove me to slit my wrists in the bathtub on the eve of his final strike against my father. Yet when my ghost was forced to linger by his side for seven final days, Dante stumbled upon the blood-soaked bathtub, a hidden seven-week ultrasound of the baby I lost on our anniversary, my ten-year-old high school love letter, and the horrifying confession from Camilla's own greedy parents that shattered his entire world. Watch as the untouchable syndicate boss goes mad digging through a garbage dump at 4 AM for our wedding rings and begs on his knees outside the mortuary for a wife who will never return.
